purpose: Belumosudil is used to treat a condition called chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) in adults and children 12 years and older. This is a complication that can happen after a stem cell or bone marrow transplant, where the donated cells attack the patient's own body. It is used when at least two other treatments have already been tried.
how_it_works: Your immune system can sometimes overreact after a transplant, causing inflammation and damage to your own tissues. Belumosudil works by blocking a specific protein in the body called ROCK2, which helps calm down this overactive immune response. By doing this, it helps reduce the symptoms and damage caused by graft-versus-host disease.
common_side_effects: Infections, feeling tired or weak, nausea, diarrhea, shortness of breath, cough, swelling in the arms or legs, muscle or joint pain, headache, stomach pain, and low levels of certain blood cells. You may also notice changes in some of your lab values like liver enzymes or blood counts.
warnings: Belumosudil can cause serious infections, so tell your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, or signs of infection. It can also affect your liver, so regular blood tests are needed to monitor liver function. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should not use this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby or a nursing infant. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of this drug in your body.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 200 mg taken by mouth twice a day with food. Your doctor may adjust or temporarily stop your dose depending on how you tolerate the medication or if you experience side effects. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
